q: Which printed document sets out the procedural and administrative terms of the contract?
n: The general conditions are the printed document of the contract's procedural and administrative terms. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); AIA A201.

q: Guarantee the quality of materials and workmanship performed.
n: A guarantee (warranty) bond guarantees the quality of materials and workmanship for a period after completion. Source: RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 62; UAP SPP Doc. 201.

q: What is a preset sum the contractor pays for delays?
n: Liquidated damages are a preset sum the contractor pays for each day of delay, agreed in advance in the contract. Source: Civil Code, Art. 2226; RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 68.

q: Letter needed for demolition.
n: A demolition permit application is accompanied by a letter of intent stating the owner's plan to demolish, along with other permit requirements. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III (demolition permit requirements).

q: 1st step for building permit processing.
n: Building permit processing starts with the barangay clearance for the site. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III; LGU OBO permit checklists.

q: 2nd step for building permit processing.
n: The second step is the locational clearance, conformance with the CLUP and zoning ordinance. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III; HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: 3rd step for building permit processing.
n: The item's third step, zoning, is the zoning administrator's clearance confirming the use is allowed in the zone. Source: LGU OBO permit checklists; HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: 4th step for building permit processing.
n: With clearances in hand, the owner files the application for the building permit with the plans. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: Responsible for the issuance of electrical permits.
n: Electrical permits are issued by the city or municipal hall, through the OBO. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III (ancillary permits).

q: Whatcolor is the envelope for commercial projects?
n: Many OBOs use coloured folders or envelopes to sort permit applications by use. Red is the common colour for commercial projects. Colours vary by LGU, so confirm with the local OBO. Source: LGU OBO filing practice (no NBC provision).

q: What color is the envelope for residential projects?
n: In common OBO practice, residential permit applications go in yellow folders or envelopes. Confirm with the local OBO. Source: LGU OBO filing practice (no NBC provision).

q: What color is the envelope for industrial projects?
n: In common OBO practice, industrial permit applications go in violet folders or envelopes. Confirm with the local OBO. Source: LGU OBO filing practice (no NBC provision).

q: Whatcolor is the envelope for institutional projects?
n: In common OBO practice, institutional permit applications go in blue folders or envelopes. Confirm with the local OBO. Source: LGU OBO filing practice (no NBC provision).

q: Which does NOT go on the cover sheet of an architectural set?
n: The cover sheet carries the title block, sheet index, vicinity and location plan and general notes. The roof plan is a regular drawing sheet. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (architectural documents).

q: What security does the contractor post to guarantee the work will be done per the contract?
n: A performance bond guarantees the contractor will complete the work as the contract requires, protecting the owner against default. Source: RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 39; UAP SPP Doc. 201.

q: The amount retained by the owner shall be released how many months after the date of the final payment?
n: Retention money (commonly 10% of each progress billing) is released to the contractor after the guarantee period following final payment, commonly 3 months. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 201 practice; RA 9184 IRR, Annex E (retention).

q: How many months is the retention period where the contractor should address defects after turnover of construction?
n: After turnover, the contractor must correct defects reported within the defects period, here 2 months. Projects set the period in the general conditions. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions), correction of work after completion.

q: In preparation of the contract documents, the architect should always consider and include in the contract the following provisions except one:
n: Contracts should set out dispute steps (negotiation, mediation, arbitration). An "out-of-court settlement" is an outcome, not a contract provision. Source: RA 9285 (ADR Act of 2004); EO 1008 (CIAC).

q: In labor-materials ratio, what is the most common ratio used in the Philippine setting in coming up with an estimate?
n: Philippine estimates commonly split cost into about 70% materials and 30% labour. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate; common Philippine estimating practice.

q: Acease-and-desist order is issued by the office of the building official on any construction activity upon the issuance of:
n: Under the NBC enforcement procedure, the Building Official issues a cease-and-desist (work stoppage) order when notices of violation go unheeded, here after the third notice. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 207–212 (violations and penalties).

q: What is to be secured first before excavation for a basement?
n: Excavation for a basement needs an excavation (accessory) permit before digging starts. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: Contract documents should be signed in how many copies by both the contractor and the client duly witnessed.
n: Contract documents are usually signed by owner and contractor in triplicate before witnesses: one copy each for owner, contractor and architect. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 201.

q: Who checks the accuracy of a subcontractor's shop drawings before they go to the architect?
n: The general contractor reviews and checks subcontractors' shop drawings for accuracy before passing them to the architect. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); AIA A201 Sec. 3.12.

q: Which of these is NOT an ancillary permit?
n: Ancillary permits cover architectural, civil/structural, electrical, mechanical, sanitary, plumbing and electronics work. Fencing needs an accessory permit. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: If the builder doesn't own the lot, what must he submit for a building permit?
n: If the applicant does not own the lot, he submits the lot owner's notarized written consent, plus a copy of the lease or contract. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: A written statement from the architect confirming the amount due to the contractor for work accomplished.
n: The architect certifies the value of work accomplished and the amount due to the contractor. The item calls this a certificate of completion; in AIA usage it is the Certificate for Payment. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202 (construction phase); AIA G702.

q: Which of these cannot issue a construction (surety) bond?
n: Construction (surety) bonds come from licensed surety or insurance companies (Prudential Guarantee, UCPB General Insurance, MAPFRE). Bail bond agents deal only with criminal bail. Source: Insurance Commission rules; Insurance Code (PD 612 as amended).

q: Which is NOT signed and sealed by the architect?
n: The architect signs and seals the architectural plans, specifications and bill of materials as submitted sets. In this item's framing the roof plan is not a separately signed document. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20; NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 302.

q: What makes a building permit void?
o: Work not started within a year of issuance
Work stopped for a year for lack of funds
n: A building permit becomes void if work does not start within one year of issuance, or is suspended or abandoned for 120 days. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 305.

q: "Bid" and ______ mean the same.
n: "Tender" is the British and international term for a bid. Source: Merriam-Webster; FIDIC Procurement Procedures Guide.

q: How is design-build commonly rendered?
n: Design-build is commonly done "by administration," with the architect managing construction for the owner at cost plus a fee, or for a guaranteed maximum cost. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 208 (Design-Build Services).

q: A horizontal cut about 1.2 m above the floor, looking down at walls and fixtures, is a:
n: A floor plan is a horizontal section cut about 1.2 m above the floor, looking down at walls, openings and fixtures. Source: Ching, Architectural Graphics.

q: Which body acts on zoning exceptions, reclassification or changes to the zoning ordinance?
n: Zoning exceptions, reclassifications and amendments to the zoning ordinance are acted on by the city or municipal council (Sanggunian), the local legislature. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 458/447; HLURB/DHSUD Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: What is a fully signed offer to do the work the project calls for?
n: A bid is only an offer. Once accepted and signed by both parties, the offer to do the work becomes the contract. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1305 and 1319.

q: Who issues building permits in an LGU?
n: The Building Official, head of the LGU's Office of the Building Official, issues building permits. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 205 and 301.
